top_temples.name: Ahobila Narasimha Swamy Temple (Upper Ahobilam)
top_temples.location_note: The principal shrine of the Nava Narasimha (nine-temple) Ahobilam complex, on a hill in Kurnool district; site where Narasimha is believed to have slain Hiranyakashipu.

top_temples.name: Prahalada Varada / Bhargava Narasimha Temple (Lower Ahobilam)
top_temples.location_note: Situated below the hill, about 8 km from Upper Ahobilam; one of the other Nava Narasimha shrines, more accessible for daily worship.

top_temples.name: Amaralingeswara Temple (Amareswara Temple)
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Krishna River; one of the five Pancharama Kshetras of Shiva, houses a 15-ft marble Shiva linga with consort Goddess Bala Chamundika.

top_temples.name: Mahishasura Mardini and Veerabhadraswamy Shrine Circle
top_temples.location_note: Subsidiary shrine circle within the same Amareswara temple complex, alongside Omkareswara Swamy and Guru Dattatreya shrines; noted here as the complex's second most distinct devotional focus.

top_temples.name: Sri Anantheswara Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Penna River in Anantapur city; one of the two most important temples in the city, gave the city part of its name.

top_temples.name: Sri Anjaneya Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: Also on the banks of the Penna River in Anantapur city, alongside Anantheswara Temple.

top_temples.name: Veerabhadra Temple, Lepakshi
top_temples.location_note: Lepakshi, Anantapur district; renowned Vijayanagara-era temple famed for its hanging pillar and giant monolithic Nandi.

top_temples.name: Sri Ranganatha Swamy Temple, Penukonda
top_temples.location_note: Penukonda, Anantapur district; noted for its architectural grandeur.

top_temples.name: Hemavati Shiva Temple
top_temples.location_note: Hemavati, Anantapur district; built by the Nolamba dynasty between the 8th-11th centuries.

top_temples.name: Sri Veera Venkata Satyanarayana Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: On Ratnagiri Hill; regarded as the second most prominent pilgrimage temple in Andhra Pradesh after Tirumala, rebuilt in 1933-34.

top_temples.name: Vana Durga and Kanaka Durga Temples
top_temples.location_note: Local protective Devi shrines situated on the same Ratnagiri hill range as the main Satyanarayana temple.

top_temples.name: Sri Bhimeswara Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the five Pancharama Kshetras of Shiva in Andhra Pradesh; 9th-century temple with a 9-floor, 120-ft gopuram in East Godavari district.

top_temples.name: Kashi Vishweshwara Swamy Shrine
top_temples.location_note: Subsidiary shrine within the Bhimeswara temple premises, facing south, alongside other sub-shrines to Ganapathi and Annapurna.

top_temples.name: Kotappakonda Trikoteswara Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: On a hill about 13 km southwest of Narasaraopet, Guntur district; named for three hills representing Brahma, Vishnu, and Maheshwara.

top_temples.name: Ankamma Thalli Temple
top_temples.location_note: Within Guntur city; a prominent local Devi shrine of deep cultural significance to residents.

top_temples.name: Sri Anjaneya Swamy Temple, Ponnur
top_temples.location_note: Ponnur, Guntur district; built in 1969, known for a 24-ft granite Hanuman statue and a 30-ft Garuda shrine.

top_temples.name: Bhavanarayana Swamy Temple, Bapatla
top_temples.location_note: Bapatla, Guntur district; one of five Bhavanarayana temples in Andhra Pradesh.

top_temples.name: Chaturmukha Brahma and Nageswara Swamy Temple, Chebrole
top_temples.location_note: Chebrole village, about 10 miles south of Guntur city; notable for its rare four-faced Brahma idol.

top_temples.name: Sri Raghavendra Swamy Brindavanam, Mantralayam
top_temples.location_note: On the Tungabhadra river in Kurnool district; site where the saint entered Jeeva Samadhi in 1671, a major pilgrimage centre.

top_temples.name: Yaganti Uma Maheswara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Yaganti, Kurnool district; 5th-6th century temple with a single-stone Ardhanareeswara idol and a slowly-growing Nandi statue.

top_temples.name: Shirdi Sai Baba Temple
top_temples.location_note: Star-shaped temple on the Tungabhadra river banks, Kurnool; known as 'South Shirdi', considered the oldest Sai Baba temple.

top_temples.name: Jagannatha Gattu Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kurnool district; ancient temple noted for stone carvings and an undeciphered script on its walls.

top_temples.name: Saraswati Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kurnool district; a rare temple dedicated to the goddess of learning, depicted with four arms in Padmasana.

top_temples.name: Sri Panakala Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop the hill in Mangalagiri; one of the 8 Mahakshetrams of Vishnu, famous for the self-manifested deity accepting Panakam (jaggery water) offerings.

top_temples.name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (foot of the hill)
top_temples.location_note: At the base of the same hill in Mangalagiri; believed installed by Yudhisthira, has one of South India's tallest gopurams.

top_temples.name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple (Talpagiri)
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Pennar river in Nellore city; over 600 years old, marked by a 29-metre Galigopuram with seven gold kalasams.

top_temples.name: Sri Narasimhaswamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 13 km from Nellore city centre; dedicated to Vishnu's fourth incarnation.

top_temples.name: Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy Kamakshi Temple, Jonnawada
top_temples.location_note: Jonnawada, about 12 km from Nellore, on the bank of the Pennar river.

top_temples.name: Sri Shiva Temple
top_temples.location_note: Listed among Nellore's well-known city temples.

top_temples.name: Sri Rajarajeshwari Temple
top_temples.location_note: A notable Devi temple within Nellore city.

top_temples.name: Markandeya Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Godavari river in Rajahmundry; considered the city's oldest temple, popular during Mahashivratri.

top_temples.name: Mahakaleshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Rajahmundry; known locally for its Bhasma Aarti ritual.

top_temples.name: Kotilingeswara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Rajahmundry; houses numerous Shiva lingas placed by generations of devotees around a large central linga.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple (Sri Sri Radha Gopinath Dasavatara Temple)
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Godavari in Rajahmundry; a major modern spiritual and cultural landmark.

top_temples.name: Venu Gopala Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: Rajahmundry city; known for its grand annual celebrations.

top_temples.name: Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: On Simhachalam Hill within Visakhapatnam GVMC; the second-largest temple in Andhra Pradesh after Tirumala, with inscriptions dating to the 11th century.

top_temples.name: Kasi Vishweswara Sub-shrine, Simhachalam Temple Complex
top_temples.location_note: A subsidiary shrine within the same Varaha Narasimha temple complex, alongside sub-shrines to Rama, Anjaneya, and Andal; noted here since no separate major standalone temple exists distinct to Simhachalam itself.

top_temples.name: Sri Kalahasteeswara Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the Pancha Bhoota Sthalas representing air (Vayu); associated with the legend of the devotee Kannappa.

top_temples.name: Sri Subrahmanya Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the centre of Srikalahasti town, reached via about 150 steps; a distinct major shrine from the main Kalahasteeswara temple.

top_temples.name: Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Krishna River in the Nallamala Hills; one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and one of the eighteen Shakti Peethas, a rare dual-status shrine.

top_temples.name: Sikhareswara Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the highest point of the Srisailam hilly region; a distinct hilltop Shiva shrine separate from the main Mallikarjuna temple.

top_temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Temple, Tirumala
top_temples.location_note: Atop the Tirumala hills; one of the world's most-visited pilgrimage sites and richest temples, the city's defining shrine.

top_temples.name: Sri Padmavathi Ammavari Temple, Tiruchanur
top_temples.location_note: About 5 km from Tirupati town centre; pilgrims traditionally visit here before ascending Tirumala.

top_temples.name: Sri Govindaraja Swami Temple
top_temples.location_note: In Tirupati town itself; features a seven-storied entrance tower with Vaishnava iconography.

top_temples.name: Sri Kapileswara Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 3 km north of Tirupati at the foot of the Tirumala hills; the only major Shiva temple in Tirupati.

top_temples.name: Kapila Theertham
top_temples.location_note: Adjacent to Kapileswara Swamy Temple in Tirupati; a Saivite temple and sacred waterfall theertham.

top_temples.name: Sri Kanaka Durga Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop Indrakeeladri Hill in Vijayawada; one of India's Shaktipeethas, depicts the goddess in her Mahishasurmardini form.

top_temples.name: Sri Subramanya Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the foot of Indrakeeladri Hill; one of Vijayawada's oldest temples, built in the 17th century by King Madhava Varma.

top_temples.name: Sri Venkateshwara Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the most-visited temples within Vijayawada city.

top_temples.name: Sri Vyagra Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Agiripalli
top_temples.location_note: Agiripalli, about 25 km from Vijayawada; tradition holds it to be roughly 4,000 years old per the Puranas.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Krishna River in Vijayawada; a three-storied modern temple with marble idols.

top_temples.name: Sri Kanaka Maha Lakshmi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Considered the presiding deity temple of Visakhapatnam city; current structure built in the early 20th century.

top_temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Rushikonda
top_temples.location_note: Atop Rushikonda Hill in Visakhapatnam; a modern 10-acre temple built by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams.

top_temples.name: Sri Shirdi Sai Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Chinna Waltair, Visakhapatnam; houses multiple deities including Ganapati, Shiva, and Dattatreya alongside Sai Baba.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple, Visakhapatnam
top_temples.location_note: One of the city's largest religious compounds; established 2005 with marble idols.

top_temples.name: Sri Visweswara Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: A well-known city temple in Visakhapatnam distinct from the hilltop Simhachalam shrine.
